text:
luca: Heads-up from onboarding: our "adaptive batching" in the Python and JS sampleapps caused a quota blitz against gateway quotas during a customer bulk-embed run. Seeing lots of 429s.

luca: Repro in staging: run the sample import tool against ~1M small documents with default sampler (adaptive_batch=true, max_batch_bytes=1MB), concurrency=16, paginator prefetch=4. After steady-state we see sudden spikes of 429s and then retries that worsen the window.

priya: Can you paste the sample call pattern?

luca: Sure:
```python
p = Redwood.Paginator("/v1/embeds", page_size=200, prefetch=4)
batcher = AdaptiveBatcher(max_bytes=1_000_000)
for page in p:
    for item in page:
        batcher.add(item)
    if batcher.ready():
        client.embed_batch(batcher.flush())
```

luca: AdaptiveBatcher was trying to pack many small docs into large requests to be token-efficient. Problem: gateway has per-tenant concurrent-request soft limits (and per-route token throughput), so many clients sending large batches concurrently hit server-side quota checks and get 429s.

tom: Why did adaptive batching amplify the problem vs naive batching?

luca: Two reasons: (1) Larger batches take longer server-side so concurrency window widens; (2) the Paginator prefetch + batcher means multiple in-flight large requests overlap. So rather than 16 small fast requests you get 16 large slow ones that saturate a quota dimension (tokens/sec or per-request CPU).

erin: Does retry behavior contribute? I bet retry middleware retries immediately for POSTs with exponential backoff but small base so retries align and spike.

priya: Confirmed in logs: `2026-07-12T09:14:01Z gateway 429 quota_exceeded tenant=acct-new concurrent=22 path=/v1/embeds tokens=1.2M`. Retries then queued, we see a secondary spike ~8s later.

tom: Workarounds documented for customers?

luca: Quick mitigations we pushed to sampleapp: set adaptive_batch=false by default for onboarding, lower max_batch_bytes to 256KB, and recommend `prefetch=1`/`concurrency=4` for bulk imports during first run. That immediately reduced spike amplitude in staging.

erin: SDK-level fixes we should pursue: (A) add per-route concurrency accounting to AdaptiveBatcher so it won't issue >N concurrent batches for a route; (B) expose a soft throttler/token-bucket in the SDK that respects tenant quota hints (we can use Retry-After and a RateLimitEvent hook); (C) change retry middleware to full jitter and increase min backoff for POSTs that return 429.

priya: Also propose adding a "server-cost-estimate" field to responses (header) so SDK can estimate cost of a batch and avoid issuing batches that would exceed local per-window budget. Might be infra/contract work though.

infra-bot: noted: infra ticket created infra/429-guidance-912 - consider adding quota hint headers (estimated_cost, tenant_window_ms).

tom: For parity: JS and Py adaptive batchers share logic but differ in concurrency primitives. We'll need patches in both SDKs + updates to sampleapp templates. Let's make an action list.

priya: Action list: 1) immediate sampleapp defaults -> adaptive_batch=false + doc note; 2) SDK change: per-route concurrency cap + backpressure hook; 3) retry middleware: full jitter + higher base for POST 429s; 4) infra: explore quota hint headers; 5) CI: add smoke test simulating large-batch overlap to detect regressions.

luca: QA: can you add an integration test that runs the importer with fake quota limits and asserts no >N concurrent batches and that retries backoff with jitter?

qa-bot: Will add `BulkImport_Backpressure` test to SDK CI. It will fake a throttling proxy that returns 429 + Retry-After and assert the client spreads retries.

erin: I'll open PRs for py-sdk & js-sdk to add a simple in-process per-route semaphore and a RateLimitEvent callback. Also bump default sampleapp batch size.

priya: Thanks. Let's also add a one-liner to the onboarding checklist: "For large imports, disable adaptive batching until you confirm tenant throughput thresholds or consult Support."

luca: Great triage team. Marking follow-up to verify after PRs and two staging ramps. :thumbsup:
